name: Basilica of St. Adalbert
history: Polish immigrants founded the parish in 1881 and built a small wooden church. The cornerstone of the present church was laid on 18 August 1907 and work went on until 1913. It was named a basilica in 1979 and dedicated as one in 1980, for the parish centennial.
arch: Romanesque Revival by Henry J. Harks, faced in Sandusky limestone with Bedford limestone trim. Its two towers are 134 feet high and its central dome rises to 150 feet.
features: The dome shows Byzantine influence, and the large rose window shows Gothic influence.
Edmund Verlinden designed the altars, pulpit, font and confessionals.

look.d: At 150 feet, the dome made this one of the tallest buildings in Grand Rapids.
A Gothic touch on a Romanesque front.

fun: St. Adalbert, the patron, is a patron saint of Poland, the homeland of the founding families.
journal: Polish Grand Rapids built itself a dome. Three styles in one stone face.
